clue.text: Ugly thing, thorny area with trees

parts.note: an orc is a hideous goblin-like creature of fantasy fiction
a thorny problem is a hard one, difficult to deal with

explanation.surface: A grim, prickly patch of woodland described in a gardener's grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot planted with fruit trees is exactly an area with trees, the plain dictionary sense.

clue.text: French bottom pinched in lift styled like a toilet? What mademoiselle might exclaim

indicators.note: pinched in means squeezed inside another piece
in a down clue lifting something raises it, so the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the French phrase a la means in the style of
loo is British slang for a toilet

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A cheeky French scene: a bottom pinched in a lift decorated like a lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'lift' reads the letters upwards; 'à la' is French for 'in the style of', and loo is British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: This French exclamation of surprise or saucy appreciation is just what a young Frenchwoman might cry out.

clue.text: Furniture on display, half of both inside pack, say?

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a pack is an example of a set of playing cards, hence the say
something up is on display, as with a notice put up

indicators.note: half of the word means its first two of four letters

explanation.surface: Furniture displayed in a shop, half of which goes into a flat-pack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Furniture on display' looks like the definition, but 'on display' belongs to the wordplay; a pack is a deck of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabinets with shelves and doors for storing things are pieces of household furniture.

clue.text: Abroad — not very far?

definitions.meaning: abroad in the old sense of going about, in circulation, as in rumours abroad
a distance of twelve inches, as in 'only a foot away', is not far at all

explanation.surface: Going overseas, yet barely travelling any distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something underway or circulating, like a plot, is said to be abroad; and a single foot is a tiny distance.

clue.text: Periods without a drink, a cause of internal discomfort

indicators.note: without first suggests the letter is taken out of the periods; it then reappears at the very end

parts.note: days are periods of time
Pepsi is a brand of soft drink
taken as written

explanation.surface: Going for long stretches without a drink can upset the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periods' reads as menstrual periods in the surface, but here it means spans of time; 'without' moves a letter out of the first word to the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigestion is a stomach complaint, an upset of the digestive system felt inside the body.

clue.text: Only a proportion taken from income, a tax evaded is a dangerous thing

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, so the letters run on inside them across the word breaks

explanation.surface: Tax dodging, paying on only part of your income, is risky business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only a proportion taken from' says the letters sit inside 'income, a tax evaded'; 'is' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher's cleaver for chopping carcasses is a heavy sharp blade, plainly a hazardous tool.

clue.text: Leading European state

parts.note: main means leading or chief

explanation.surface: A leading European country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a European nation but is a US one.
explanation.definitionFit: The north-eastern US state on the Atlantic coast is one of the fifty states of America.

clue.text: Possible treatment, mixture of tisane and rum

indicators.note: a mixture of letters is a jumble, so the words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A home remedy: herbal tea mixed with rum.
explanation.walkthrough: A tisane is a herbal tea; only it is jumbled, and rum stays as it is at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood serum containing antibodies is given to fight infection or poison, so it is one possible treatment.

clue.text: Harmony always around US institute

indicators.note: around means the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: ay, or aye, is an old word for always or ever
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: There is always harmony around an American university.
explanation.walkthrough: Ay (also spelt aye) is an old poetic word for always, as in 'for ay'.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly relations and goodwill between people or nations mean living in harmony.

clue.text: Scar absolutely obvious initially, right within focus of seer?

indicators.note: within means these pieces are placed inside the other
the focus of a word is its centre, the middle letters

parts.note: yes, absolutely is an emphatic agreement

indicators.note: initially means the first letter is used

explanation.surface: A seer peers at a scar that is plainly obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'focus' of seer is its centre, the two middle letters; the question mark flags this playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A blot on the landscape, something ugly to look at, is what a scar on scenery would be called.

clue.text: Muddy beast, one very quietly entering house

indicators.note: one piece going into another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quietly

explanation.surface: Someone tiptoes into a house, and the clue calls the intruder a mud-caked animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus wallows in rivers and mud, so a muddy beast describes it vividly.

clue.text: Very good trip is taken round outskirts of Llanelli

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed round the other piece, enclosing it
to trip is to stumble, so the letters of the words that follow are knocked out of order
the outskirts of a town are its edges, so the first and last letters of the place name are used

explanation.surface: A holiday trip that takes in the edge of the Welsh town of Llanelli.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' rearranges IS TAKEN into SAINTKE, and 'round' wraps that around LI, the outside letters of Llanelli, a town in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone behaving like a holy person is extremely virtuous, so the phrase very good fits.

clue.text: Hearty: he contrived to embrace old sailor's greeting

indicators.note: embracing means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other
something contrived is artificially put together, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hearty fellow manages to hug an old seadog, as shipmates do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearty' looks like a description of the sailor, but it is anagram fodder; 'old sailor' is not a unit, since 'old' gives a letter and 'sailor's greeting' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The nautical hail used to call to another vessel or person is a seafarer's traditional way of saying hello.

clue.text: Authority that doesn't speak?

definitions.meaning: the right to give permission or make decisions, as in 'on whose word?'
split differently, the letters read as a verb of speech followed by O, zero, so one who utters nothing

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a powerful figure who stays silent.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: break the answer as SAYS plus O, the letter that looks like zero, and it describes someone who utters nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the final word on a matter, the right to approve or forbid, is a colloquial term for authority.

clue.text: For starters, Andre Agassi rather gloriously hairless — I'm tearing my hair out!

definitions.text: For starters, Andre Agassi rather gloriously hairless — I'm tearing my hair out!

indicators.note: starters are the opening items, so the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A frustrated cry about the famously bald tennis star Andre Agassi.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of five words spell a cry of exasperation, which the clue's last part also defines; Agassi famously shaved his head.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation is the noise of despair one makes when frustrated enough to pull at one's own head.

clue.text: Stock cut, foreign currency held up

indicators.note: held means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: hacked means cut roughly

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: the yen is the currency of Japan

explanation.surface: A financial report: stock cut, foreign currency held up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' means a stock phrase, clichéd; 'up' reverses YEN to NEY, 'held' in HACKED.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock expression is trite and overused, which is exactly what a worn-out, clichéd phrase is.

clue.text: Strong bonds formed with this guru, sleep disturbed

indicators.note: sleep that is disturbed is broken up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A spiritual guru whose sleep is interrupted forms strong bonds with followers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges GURU and SLEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: An extremely strong adhesive makes powerful joints, so it is what tight bonds are made with.

clue.text: Dog keeping busy, originally sniffing female's bottom

indicators.note: busy suggests bustling activity, so the letters are shuffled about
originally means the first letter of the word
the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A dog keeps busy, sniffing a female's rear end as dogs do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' rearranges KEEPING; 'originally sniffing' gives S and 'female's bottom' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: A small toy breed with a flat face and long coat, from China, is a kind of dog.

clue.text: Logical thinker abandoned sheikhdom — Noah!

parts.note: left means abandoned or deserted

indicators.note: Noah is read as 'no' plus the exclamation 'ah', meaning that exclamation is dropped

parts.note: Bahrain is a Gulf state ruled as a kingdom with sheikhs

explanation.surface: Noah's exasperated cry on leaving a Gulf state, as if fleeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noah' is split as 'no AH', removing AH from BAHRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The hemisphere popularly linked with logic and analysis is jokingly called the logical thinking part of the mind.

clue.text: Funny straight man split

definitions.note: used as a noun, a funny is a joke

parts.note: Ernie Wise was the straight man in the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise
a crack is a split or fissure

explanation.surface: A comedy partnership in which the funny one and the straight man break up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' is a noun here, meaning a joke; Morecambe and Wise were a much-loved British TV comedy double act.
explanation.definitionFit: A quip or clever joke is something said to be funny, and a funny is informal for a joke.

clue.text: The Japanese keep doing it, for crying out loud!

indicators.note: out loud means spoken, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: wailing is crying loudly

explanation.surface: An exasperated protest at a nation's persistent habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for crying out loud' is a stock exclamation; here 'out loud' signals that WAILING (crying) sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan continues to hunt whales commercially despite international protest, so this is what it keeps on doing.

clue.text: Cakes to drop in fumbles

indicators.note: dropping a piece means leaving it out of the word

parts.note: muffins are small cakes
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone clumsily drops cakes while handling them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to drop' removes IN from MUFFINS.
explanation.definitionFit: To bungle a catch or a task is to handle it clumsily, which is what fumbling means.

clue.text: Colour ranges: traces possibly including pink, primarily

indicators.note: including means the first piece holds the second within it
possibly says the letters could be in another order
primarily means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A paint chart: traces of colour, perhaps including pink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges TRACES and 'including' puts P (first of pink) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bands of colours spread out as by a prism are ranges of colour, the plural of spectrum.

clue.text: Tree a waste, cut

indicators.note: a cut word loses its end, here the final letter

parts.note: to spend money is to use it up, or waste it

explanation.surface: A tree is a waste of space and should be cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes the last letter of SPEND.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a poplar with trembling leaves, one particular kind of tree.

clue.text: Have fun on a Spanish beach

parts.note: to play is to have fun

explanation.surface: Enjoying yourself on holiday on a Spanish beach.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for a beach or shore, familiar from names like Playa de las Americas, is a Spanish beach.

clue.text: Swindle firm for a nicker?

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
something firm is steady or secure

explanation.surface: A fraudster cons a company to pocket a nicker, slang for a pound coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nicker' looks like British slang for a pound, but here it is one who nicks, that is, arrests: a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to nick is to arrest, so the police officer who does so is jokingly one who nicks.

clue.text: Fancy redhead in Neanderthal's place?

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a cave was the home of a Neanderthal, a prehistoric human
the head of the word red is its first letter

explanation.surface: Did a caveman fancy a redhead?
explanation.walkthrough: 'redhead' is read as the head of 'red', giving R inside CAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for or desire something strongly is to fancy it, as a verb.

clue.text: Salutation at a wedding breakfast, possibly?

definitions.meaning: a speech and raised glasses honouring the couple
grilled bread is a breakfast staple, so it could be breakfast

explanation.surface: A tribute raised at the wedding breakfast, the meal after the ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'wedding breakfast' is the British term for the reception meal; the clue splits it across two readings.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinking to someone's health is a salutation, and browned bread is a common morning meal.

clue.text: Silly welcoming corrupt leader in backward state, moreover

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: inane means silly or senseless

indicators.note: one letter is placed inside the other piece
backward means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: to state is to say

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A foolish ruler welcomes a crooked boss in a backward country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward state' suggests an undeveloped country, but 'state' is the verb to say, read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'besides' or 'anyway', adding a further point, just as moreover does.

clue.text: A little bit separate

parts.note: a part is a portion or little bit of something

explanation.surface: A small piece kept separate from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Things kept at a distance from each other are separate, an adverb used predicatively as in 'live separately'.

clue.text: Noble rank inspiring baron finally, last in line

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: a grade is a rank or level

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word is used
the last letter in the word is taken

explanation.surface: A noble rank that brings a baron in, the last one in the line of succession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' puts N, the last letter of baron, into GRADE; 'last in line' adds E.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish or Portuguese nobleman of the highest rank, and loosely any distinguished person, is a noble.

clue.text: Independence ultimately ain't so bad for the country

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of the word is used
bad here signals the letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A nation decides that, in the end, independence is not such a bad thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives E, the end of Independence, and 'bad' rearranges AIN'T SO.
explanation.definitionFit: This Baltic state, which regained independence in 1991, is a country of northern Europe.
